title: Spelunk protocol
description: Single source of truth for every type that crosses a process boundary: the parsed query (ParsedQuery), the messages between the search panel webview and the extension host, and the JSON-RPC methods between the extension host and the daemon. Run `node protocol/gen.mjs` after editing.

Span.description: Span is a range of UTF-16 offsets into the raw query text.

MessageLine.description: MessageLine is one line of a commit message, with what the query's text terms match in it.

SpanLine.description: SpanLine is a later line of a code match that spans lines, with the part of the match on it (and any other term's matches there).

Range.description: Range is a range of UTF-16 offsets into the text shown on screen.

Hit.description: Hit is a matched Range plus the text term that matched, which picks its highlight color.

hole.description: For a struct: match, the number of the template hole whose code this marks (1 for the first name in the template); absent where the template's own code matched.

HoleValue.description: HoleValue is the code a struct: template's named hole took in one match, its space squeezed and cut short when long.

hole.description: The hole's number, as in Hit.hole.

OpName.description: OpName is an operator's name, the part before the colon.

CaseSetting.description: CaseSetting is how capital letters match when the query has no case: ignored (off), matched (on), or matched only when the query has a capital letter (smart).

ResultOrder.description: ResultOrder is how current files are sorted: best match first, or by repo, path and line.

RankReason.description: RankReason is why best-match order put a file where it is: it defines a searched name or is open in the editor, or it was moved down as a test, vendored or generated file. Absent when nothing stands out or the order is path.

SinceRevision.description: SinceRevision is how a file found at a revision differs in the current files: its content changed, or it was deleted.

Match.description: Match says how a value was written: bare (literal), quoted (phrase), /regex/, a path glob such as *.go (f: and repo: only), or a struct: template of code with :[holes] (structural).

Mode.description: Mode is what a query searches: current files or Git history.

Severity.description: Severity is how serious a Diagnostic is; only errors stop a search.

TextEdit.description: TextEdit replaces a span of the query text.

Fix.description: Fix is a titled set of edits that repairs or rewrites the query.

Diagnostic.description: Diagnostic is a problem the parser found, with fixes the user can apply.

Resolved.description: Resolved is a friendlier label for an operator value, such as an author's full name.

Node.description: Node is one node of the parsed query tree.

contentOnly.description: true for a content: or struct: term, which matches the text of files (or a commit's changed lines) and never file names or commit messages.

Globals.description: Globals are the query-wide operators case:, word:, count:, type:, order: and at:, or null when absent.

case.description: the query's case: value: yes, no or smart (match case only when the query has a capital letter).

word.description: the query's word: value, yes or no; absent when the query doesn't say.

order.description: the query's order: value, best or path; absent when the query doesn't say.

at.description: the query's at: value as written: the tag, branch, commit or time whose files it searches; absent when the query doesn't say.

ParsedQuery.description: ParsedQuery is the parser's output: the query tree, its global operators and its diagnostics.

hasCapital.description: whether a text term, sym: or msg: value has a capital letter, so smart case matches case. In a regex, only literal letters count: \W and \p{Lu} don't.

Root.description: Root is a workspace folder; its id is the first 12 hex digits of sha256(path).

Settings.description: Settings are the spelunk.* settings the daemon needs.

caseSensitive.description: the spelunk.caseSensitive setting: how a query without case: treats capital letters.

wholeWord.description: the spelunk.wholeWord setting: match text terms only as whole words unless the query says word:no.

order.description: the spelunk.order setting: how a query without order: sorts current files. Absent means best.

contextLines.description: the spelunk.results.contextLines setting: how many lines each code result shows before and after its match, 0 to 3. Absent means 0.

timeLimitMs.description: the spelunk.search.timeLimitMs setting: how long one search runs before it returns what it found so far, marked truncated. Absent means 2000.

vendoredFolders.description: the spelunk.index.vendoredFolders setting: names of folders, at any depth, whose files is:vendored matches and ranking puts last. Absent means vendor, node_modules, third_party and dist.

generatedSuffixes.description: the spelunk.index.generatedSuffixes setting: endings of file names that mark files a tool wrote, for is:generated and ranking, besides a @generated or DO NOT EDIT marker near the top. Absent means .pb.go, _gen.go, .gen.go, .gen.ts, _pb2.py, _pb2_grpc.py, _pb2.pyi, .min.js and .min.css.

codeownersFiles.description: the spelunk.index.codeownersFiles setting: where to look for a repo's CODEOWNERS file, relative to its root, the first found winning. Absent means GitHub's .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS and docs/CODEOWNERS.

commitCheckSeconds.description: the spelunk.index.commitCheckSeconds setting: how often to ask Git whether HEAD moved, which brings new commits into history search and watches. Absent means 5.

LastCommit.description: LastCommit is the newest commit that touched a file.

FileStat.description: FileStat is one file changed by a commit.

SymbolKind.description: SymbolKind is what a symbol definition is.

ResultItem.description: ResultItem is one search result: a file name, a code line, a symbol or a commit.

owners.description: Who the repo's CODEOWNERS file says owns the file, as it writes them; absent when nobody does or the repo has no CODEOWNERS file.

sinceRevision.description: For a search at a revision (at:), how the file differs now: changed, or deleted since; absent when it is the same now, and in every other search.

owners.description: Who the repo's CODEOWNERS file says owns the file, as it writes them; absent when nobody does or the repo has no CODEOWNERS file.

spanLines.description: When the match spans lines (a regex with \n, or a struct: template), the lines after line that it runs onto, in order: at most 10, so a longer match ends at endLine past the last of them. Absent for a match within one line.

endLine.description: The last line a match that spans lines ends on; present with spanLines.

holes.description: For a struct: match, what each named hole of the template took, in template order, each hole once; absent otherwise.

contextBefore.description: The lines just above the match, top first, when the contextLines setting asks for them; fewer near the start of the file.

contextAfter.description: The lines just below the match (below endLine when it spans lines), when the contextLines setting asks for them; fewer near the end of the file.

sinceRevision.description: For a search at a revision (at:), how the file differs now: changed, or deleted since; absent when it is the same now, and in every other search.
For a search at a revision (at:), how the file differs now: changed, or deleted since; absent when it is the same now, and in every other search.

inMessage.description: Whether a text term matched the commit's subject or body.

bodyLine.description: The first body line a text term matched, sent when the subject has no match.

LineHits.description: LineHits are the matches on one preview line.

OutlineSymbol.description: OutlineSymbol is a definition shown in a file preview's outline.

DiffLine.description: DiffLine is one line of a diff hunk.

Hunk.description: Hunk is one hunk of a commit diff.

Ownership.description: Ownership is who owns a file by its repo's CODEOWNERS file, and which line of it says so.

owners.description: The owners, as the file writes them; empty when the deciding line names none, or no line matches.

file.description: Where the CODEOWNERS file is, relative to the repo: .github/CODEOWNERS

line.description: The line that decides, 1-based; 0 when no line matches the file.

Preview.description: Preview is the right-hand pane's content for a selected result.

focusEndLine.description: The last line of the result when its match spans lines; the preview marks focusLine to focusEndLine. Absent otherwise.

Facet.description: Facet counts a search's results by one field, biggest bucket first, for the buttons that narrow the results.

more.description: How many smaller buckets were left out

FacetBucket.description: FacetBucket is one value of a facet: how many results have it, and the filter that keeps only them.

label.description: The value as shown, e.g. payments-api, Python, src/, @acme/payments-core, Jane Doe, Sep 2026

filter.description: The filter that keeps only this bucket, as it would be typed, e.g. repo:payments-api; a - before it leaves the bucket out

HiddenNote.description: HiddenNote counts results a filter removed, with a fix that removes the filter.

Completion.description: Completion is an autocomplete suggestion; accepting it applies its edit.

detail.description: What the suggestion means, in a few words: "Last 2 hours", "Python files".

context.description: Facts that help choose it, on a second line: "Since 08:04", "14 files · payments-api, web-checkout".

note.description: A short status shown at the end of the row: "5 files changed", "Indexing 64%".

section.description: A heading shown above this suggestion; the suggestions after it, up to the next section, belong under it.

IndexState.description: IndexState is where one index of a repo stands.

RepoStatus.description: RepoStatus is the indexing state of one repo.

OpenTarget.description: OpenTarget is where opening a result goes: a file position (path, line, column, length, or to endLine and endColumn for a match that spans lines) or a commit (repoId, sha). A file at a revision (an at: result) also has revision, and opens read-only with the text of revision/text. Lines and columns are 1-based.

endLine.description: Where a match that spans lines ends: the selection runs from line and column to endLine and endColumn.

revision.description: The full sha of the commit whose version of the file opens, for an at: result.

revisionLabel.description: How the revision reads in the editor's title: the at: value (v1.0.0), or the short sha when the search is forgotten.

OpenWhere.description: OpenWhere is which editor group a result opens in, or, for a result at a revision (at:), compare: a diff of the file then against the file now.

watches.description: The watched queries, as in watch/set.

InitializeResult.description: InitializeResult reports the daemon's version and protocol.

WatchSetParams.description: WatchSetParams list the watched queries: after each history update, the daemon runs every one that searches history over the new commits.

WatchCommit.description: WatchCommit is a new commit a watched query matched.

WatchMatchedParams.description: WatchMatchedParams announce the new commits of one repo that a watched query matched, newest first; your own commits are left out. total counts them all; commits lists at most the query's count.

FileChange.description: FileChange is one file event from VS Code's watcher.

DidChangeFilesParams.description: DidChangeFilesParams forward file events from the host, a fast path ahead of the daemon's own watcher.

ParseParams.description: ParseParams ask the daemon to parse the query box.

openFiles.description: the absolute paths of the files open in editor tabs, for is:open.

ParseResult.description: ParseResult is the parsed query plus completions at the cursor.

SearchStartParams.description: SearchStartParams start (or page) a search; the daemon re-parses the text itself.

openFiles.description: the absolute paths of the files open in editor tabs, for is:open.

SearchResult.description: SearchResult ends a search after its batches.

revisions.description: For an at: search, the commit each searched repo read, in workspace order; absent otherwise.

RevisionInfo.description: RevisionInfo is the commit an at: search read in one repo: its sha and date, or why the repo has none.

sha.description: The commit's full sha; absent when the repo has no such revision.

date.description: When the commit was made (its committer date), RFC 3339; absent with sha.

problem.description: Why the repo was not searched, when it has no such revision: "v9 isn't a tag, branch or commit here", "Not a Git repository".

RevisionTextParams.description: RevisionTextParams ask for the whole text of a file a revision result names.

RevisionText.description: RevisionText is a file's whole text as it was at the revision of a result's ref.

SearchBatchParams.description: SearchBatchParams stream up to 200 results of a running search.

PreviewParams.description: PreviewParams ask for the preview of a result.

OpenResolveParams.description: OpenResolveParams ask where a result opens.

IndexStatusResult.description: IndexStatusResult is the indexing state of every repo.

RebuildParams.description: RebuildParams name the repo to rebuild, or all when repoId is absent.

ReplacePlanParams.description: ReplacePlanParams ask for every edit that replacing the query's matches in current files would make.

replacement.description: the text each match becomes; for a /regex/ term, $1 or ${name} insert what a group matched.

openFiles.description: the absolute paths of the files open in editor tabs, for is:open.

ReplaceEdit.description: ReplaceEdit replaces one match: a range of UTF-16 offsets into the whole line.

ReplaceLine.description: ReplaceLine is one line to edit: its 1-based number, its whole text as indexed (without the line end), and its edits in order.

ReplaceFile.description: ReplaceFile is one file to edit, with its absolute path.

ReplacePlan.description: ReplacePlan is every edit a replace would make. When it would make more than the daemon plans at once, truncated is set and files is empty.

Empty.description: Empty is a message with no fields.

Envelope.description: Envelope wraps every message between the webview and the extension host, in both directions.

QueryChangedMessage.description: QueryChangedMessage reports the query box after the typing delay.

asTyped.description: True when the user dismissed the suggestions (Esc or Enter): search the box exactly as typed, including the word at the cursor.

ResultSelectMessage.description: ResultSelectMessage asks for a result's preview.

ResultOpenMessage.description: ResultOpenMessage opens a result in an editor.

ResultsMoreMessage.description: ResultsMoreMessage loads the next page of results.

HelpTryMessage.description: HelpTryMessage runs an example from the help page in the search panel.

PinnedQuery.description: PinnedQuery is a query starred in the empty box, with the name it was given, if any, and whether it is watched.

watch.description: Whether new commits the query matches are announced (query watches); history queries only.

PinnedWatchMessage.description: PinnedWatchMessage starts or stops watching a pinned query for new commits.

UnseenCommits.description: UnseenCommits are the new commits a watched query matched since it last ran: how many, and their shas.

WatchStateMessage.description: WatchStateMessage says which pinned queries can be watched (those that search history) and what each watch found since its query last ran.

ContextSetMessage.description: ContextSetMessage sets how many lines each code result shows around its match (spelunk.results.contextLines).

RecentRemoveMessage.description: RecentRemoveMessage removes a query from the recent list.

ReplacePreviewMessage.description: ReplacePreviewMessage asks what replacing the query's matches with replacement would change.

ReplaceApplyMessage.description: ReplaceApplyMessage replaces the matches its preview showed; matches is how many that was, so a plan that changed since is not applied.

WelcomeStateMessage.description: WelcomeStateMessage is what the welcome page shows: the shortcut preset and what is indexed.

mac.description: Whether keys are written for a Mac (⌘P) or for Windows and Linux (Ctrl+P)

WelcomeChooseMessage.description: WelcomeChooseMessage saves one choice made on the welcome page in the user's settings.

ParseResultMessage.description: ParseResultMessage drives the chips, diagnostics, completions and toggles.

searchText.description: The text the search runs on when it leaves out the word being completed ("Results for timeout keep updating"). Absent when the whole box is searched.

SearchDoneMessage.description: SearchDoneMessage ends a search: counts, hidden notes, Load more and errors.

revisions.description: For an at: search, the commit each searched repo read, or why it has none (from SearchResult).

newCommits.description: The shas of the commits a watch found for this query since it last ran, which the results mark New.

PreviewResultMessage.description: PreviewResultMessage fills the preview pane; stale means the result no longer exists.

IndexStatusMessage.description: IndexStatusMessage drives the header dot and indexing banners.

StateRestoreMessage.description: StateRestoreMessage restores the panel's query, recent and pinned queries, and settings.

text.description: The query box's text; absent after a settings change, which leaves the box as it is.

UiSettings.description: UiSettings are the UI-facing settings the host forwards to the webview.

ReplacePlanMessage.description: ReplacePlanMessage is the preview of a replace: the edits it would make, or why it can't.

ReplaceDoneMessage.description: ReplaceDoneMessage says what a replace changed. skipped lists the files left alone because their text no longer matched the index; changed means the matches differed from the preview, so nothing was replaced.

BannerMessage.description: BannerMessage reports daemon health: restarting, stopped or cleared.

RequestCancelled.when: A newer keystroke cancelled this request

QueryInvalid.when: search/start got a query with error diagnostics

IndexNotReady.when: A repo has no index yet; partial results still stream

RefStale.when: The file or commit behind a ref is gone

IndexCorrupt.when: A shard or database failed a check; a rebuild starts on its own

Overloaded.when: The search hit its time budget and returned what it had
